charter: A watchlist that is a LEDGER, not a list of links. The list-of-links version is the fifth instance of the queue-with-no-consumer defect this repo has already measured four times (357 critic items / ~22 built · 61 DR units / 39 write-only · 21 gate artifacts / 2 with an owner verdict · 6 skills unused for 54 days with nothing in the repo able to tell). So every row carries a status that AGES and a distilled_to that must cite the video id back. Read by pipeline/scripts/video_curriculum.py and printed at every session open by plan_status. ADVISORY ONLY — learning to see never blocks a frame, and wiring it as a gate rung would earn it the same fate as every other rung nobody can satisfy on the day it ships.
how_it_was_built: 807 candidate videos harvested from YouTube's own search across 92 queries aimed at this project's named defect classes. NO URL WAS EVER WRITTEN BY A MODEL — every id came back from ytsearch, so a hallucinated link is impossible by construction. Ten independent judge lanes scored them against the G1..G10 brief; four lanes independently reported the same hole; a second harvest of 301 more videos was run at exactly that hole and eight more judges scored it. 111 rows survived.

rows.title: Interior Designer Fixes 4 People's Bedrooms | Re:Design | Architectural Digest
rows.why: Four real bedrooms critiqued out loud, in the ORDER a professional notices things. That order is the deliverable: layout/scale first, then light, then styling — which tells the builder which of its 109 open defects a client would actually see first, and therefore what the next round must fix. Transferable: adopt her noticing sequence as the render read-order, and copy the per-bedroom prescriptions (what she ADDS to a bedroom that reads bare) as candidate object classes for our own half-made frame.  ||  The only BEDROOM-specific critique in the file, and it runs the diagnosis→fix loop four times in eleven minutes, which is the highest defect-naming density per minute of any candidate. Transferable decisions map one-to-one onto our open defects: what a designer changes FIRST in a bedroom (the bed is the anchor and everything is sized off it), headboard scale relative to the bed, the nightstand+lamp pair as one unit rather than two objects, rug size and how far it must run past the bed, and bedding as LAYERS (sheet, duvet, throw, pillow tiers) — our duvet covers 43% of the bed where delivered work covers ~80%, and this is where the builder can watch someone state the correct coverage as a decision rather than a number.  ||  The only true CRITIQUE format in either file, and it critiques the exact room type we are building. Transferable decision: the ORDER in which a designer names bedroom faults out loud - what they say first, second, third when they open a bedroom photo. Four rooms in eleven minutes means four independent orderings, which is enough to extract a ranked checklist the builder can run against its own frame in the client's noticing order (bed not anchored to its wall / nightstand and lamp scale / rug too small / curtains hung low / nothing at eye level). This is the closest thing here to the outside eye that has filed every one of our 367 defects.
rows.risk: Re:Design is a remote-consult format — the 'fix' may arrive as a mood board or render rather than the executed room, so the diagnosis half is worth more than the prescription half.

rows.title: Reviewing your 3d renders - Archviz Art Critique Ep.2
rows.why: A working archviz artist (verified: nunosilva.pt, ~130k subs, Lumion/D5 instructor) critiques MANY submitted archviz images in one sitting — which is what teaches ORDER rather than a single opinion. The transferable decision is his repeated first-pass triage: he names the defect that kills the image before he names any that merely weakens it, and in archviz that is almost always (1) camera/verticals, (2) material SCALE and visible tiling, (3) light with no readable source. Item (2) is our G6 defect verbatim — wood grain that repeats and mirrors across a wall — and hearing a professional convict it out loud on someone else's frame is the closest thing in this file to convicting it on ours.  ||  The only candidate in the whole pool where a verified working archviz artist (nunosilva.pt) puts other people's finished renders on screen and convicts them out loud, one at a time. The transferable thing is not any single fix — it is his ORDER: he reads the whole frame (composition, where the eye goes, light) before he ever touches a material, and he names the defect in one sentence before proposing the change. Lift that sequence verbatim as the C1 aiming checklist the builder currently cannot produce (367 filed items, 0 from its own eye), and lift his phrasing as the missing critique vocabulary — 'no focal point', 'the material has no scale', 'nothing in the foreground' are exactly the sentences our frame needs written about it.  ||  Verified: a professional archviz artist critiques seven viewer-submitted 3D renders in 27 minutes — roughly four minutes per image, which forces him to name only the first-order defects. That ranking (what a pro says first about a CG image) is the single thing the builder cannot generate. Second independent critic voice on the same object class, so items that appear in both his list and VizAcademy's are the ones to promote into a standing gate checklist.
rows.risk: Lumion/D5-centric: some prescriptions will be post-processing presets with no Cycles equivalent, and he also produces AI-archviz content, so a stretch may drift into tooling. Take the naming, discard the knob.

rows.title: The Do and Don'ts of Visual Merchandising with Debbie Flowerday
rows.why: The strongest credential in the whole candidate set: Debbie Flowerday is a UAL Chelsea retail-display tutor who merchandised for Gucci, Max Mara, Topshop and Estee Lauder. Retail VM is the discipline that has actually formalised how garments sit on a rail — blocking, repeating rhythm, colour runs, and density as a DELIBERATE choice rather than a leftover. Transferable decision: give each bay one focal block instead of an even mush of garments across all 9 cells, and treat rail density as a designed number.  ||  A visual-merchandising professional naming out loud what makes a rail read wrong — density, colour blocking, facing, size runs. rows.title: Organize Your Closet Like a Stylist (The Closet Boutique Method)

rows.title: How To Professionally Fold Your Garments For Retail Display
rows.why: The only item in the harvest that teaches the folded stack as a MODULE rather than as a trick: retail folding exists to make every piece the same width and depth so a stack has a flat face, square edges and a repeating value step. That is precisely the parameter our shelf items lack — fold width derived from shelf depth minus a return, constant stack height, edge alignment front-to-front. Transferable: one fold dimension + a stack count per shelf, both buildable numbers.

rows.why: Attacks the named wood defect at its root cause rather than its symptom: realism comes from VARIATION at the scale the camera resolves, not from higher-resolution textures. The copyable decision is to stop treating the wood wall as one tiled material and instead drive per-board colour/roughness/offset variation plus contact grime where boards meet floor and wardrobe — which is precisely 'grain visibly repeats and mirrors across a wall'. rows.title: Ironing Linens for Hotel Photography    SD 480p
rows.why: The transferable decision is a REVERSAL of the builder's working assumption. Delivered interior photographs are shot on PRESSED linen — a stylist's first hour on set is spent steaming out exactly the fold energy our sim is adding. So the target for cloth is not 'more folds, more realism'; it is a near-flat field carrying a small number of DELIBERATE lines (the duvet's centre fold, the turn-down at the head, the break where a pillow sits). Concrete change: drop sim wrinkle/subdivision until the duvet reads pressed, then re-add only the two or three folds a stylist would leave. This is the direct attack on the measured 2-3.7x fold-energy defect, at its cause rather than its symptom. Verified real: Vision Quest is a hospitality photography studio with 1,500+ hotel shoots for 50+ brands, and this is their own prep training — the profession that decides what a sellable bed photo looks like, saying that linen is the first thing they fix.
rows.risk: 480p, old, and a dry commercial training reel — it may spend its time on steamer equipment and room-prep logistics rather than on the finished frame. Only 10k views, but that is a specialist channel, not a filler signal. It also shows real cloth, never CG, so the builder must do the translation to sim parameters itself.
lanes: G6 — surfaces + soft goods (texture repetition, rug edge, cloth over-crumple, duvet coverage; 3D material realism AND how a bed is really made)

rows.title: How to Tile a Texture Without Repetition - Blender Tutorial
rows.why: Two decisions for the 'wood grain repeats and mirrors across the wall' defect. (a) NEVER MIRROR: mirrored extension is the loudest CG tell there is, because the eye locates an axis of symmetry before it identifies anything else in the frame — this alone convicts our wall. (b) Break the repeat period instead of shrinking it: drive a mix/offset between two samplings of the same map with a noise at a scale LARGER than the tile, so there is no period left to find. It also hands the builder a JUDGING move it currently lacks — shrink the render to a thumbnail; if the pattern is visible at thumbnail size, the tile is too small. That is a repeatable test the lane can run on every wall and floor before a gate.
rows.risk: Dated, and it solves the case of ONE continuous tiled texture across a large surface. rows.title: How to Make A Bed | Interior Design
rows.why: A practising high-end designer building a bed on camera, which is the format the brief asks for. The transferable decision is the LAYER ORDER AND THE DROP: flat sheet turned back over the duvet at the head, duvet pulled to cover the whole mattress and drape over BOTH SIDES down toward the rail, throw across the foot third. That drape is the exact geometry behind our 43%-vs-80% coverage defect — our duvet stops at the mattress top plane, so it reads as a mat laid on a slab; hers wraps the sides, which is what makes the bed read as one soft mass rather than a box with a blanket on it. Also gives the head-end fold-back, which is what fills the gap our frame leaves between duvet edge and pillows.

rows.title: Creating the perfect rug in 20mins - Blender 4.2!
rows.why: The only candidate in the file that touches the filed defect — 'rug reads flat with no edge rollover'. Confirmed by the channel's own written version: it builds the rug SILHOUETTE first — a plane scaled and extruded to real pile thickness, top edges bevelled, corner verts lifted slightly — and only then adds hair curves. That is the whole fix stated as geometry: the rug's perimeter must be a thickened, bevelled edge with a slightly raised corner so it catches a rim of light and throws a contact shadow, instead of a zero-thickness plane with a texture. Second transferable step: unwrap and scale the UVs so the fur emits evenly, which is what stops the pile from thinning at the edges and re-flattening the silhouette the bevel just bought.
rows.risk: Published by an asset-library company, so part of it is a funnel toward their paid rugs; the title has the promo shape. Hair-curve fur is Cycles-expensive at full pile density on a room-sized rug — the builder may have to fake the field and keep only the edge geometry, which is fine, but the video will not say so.

rows.title: How to Choose the Right Rug Size | Lisa Holt Design
rows.why: Gives the number our rug has never carried. Transferable decision: a bedroom rug is sized FROM THE BED, not from the room - it must extend a fixed clear margin past both sides and past the foot of the bed, and it starts a set distance down from the headboard (typically at/behind the nightstand line) rather than being centred in the room. That converts our rug from a typed extent into a derived one: rug width = bed width + 2x margin, rug start = headboard datum + offset. It also names the legal alternative (two runners flanking the bed) for when the full rug will not fit, which is a decision, not a fix.
rows.risk: US imperial throughout (feet/inches, US rug stock sizes 8x10, 9x12). Every number needs converting to mm and re-derived against our in-frame bed, which measures as a US full 1400x1900 - so the stock-size half of the advice does not transfer, only the margin rule does.

Subtracting mattress dims from the quoted quilt dims gives the lane a per-side overhang in inches it can type into the duvet build to replace the 43% coverage.

rows.title: Lighting Calculations, Inverse Square, Cosine, Efficacy & Lumen Method for Design Explained

This is the half of the hole the ratio video does not supply — the ratio tells you what the answer should be, this tells you how to compute what you actually built. Transferable decision: predict each cell's face illuminance before rendering and file it as a pixel_claim, so a dark cell fails a number instead of surviving to a critic.

rows.title: material palettes for interiors & how to get them right
rows.why: The only candidate in either file that treats a palette as a COMPOSITION WITH PROPORTIONS rather than a list of nice materials. Applied to our frame that means the wood floor and the wood wall boards must be counted as ONE dominant material holding the 60 - not two materials each competing for a 30 - and the accent must be a MATERIAL that repeats (brass at the hang rails, the lamp bases, the hardware) rather than a colour that appears once. That re-assignment is the shape of our measured 0.300 distribution error, and it is a decision the builder can make before it renders, not after it measures.  ||  Directly answers the half of the hole that says every colour video assumes the dominant tier is PAINT. This is a MATERIAL palette video: the tiers are wood, stone, metal and textile, which is our actual condition (wood floor + wood wall boards dominating the frame). Transferable decision: rebuild the 60/30/10 declaration in material terms rather than colour terms, so the dominant 60 is legitimately 'wood, two tones, one undertone family' and the 30/10 are the tiers that must then carry contrast — which is a different repair from repainting a wall. 19 min with reasoning out loud, the sweet spot the brief asks for.

Silent Gliss is a real specification brand, so this also hands the builder a product family whose published technical data carries fold pitch, fullness ratio and stack-back tables. Transferable decision: our sheer's fold period and fold count should come from a declared wave pitch (typically 60/80 mm carrier spacing), not from a cloth sim — which directly attacks the measured 2-3.7x over-crumpling in G6.
